title: How Many Real Zeros Does a Strictly Increasing Cubic Have?
originalTopic: Counting and approximating real zeros with graphs
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For f(x) = x^3 + x + 1, decide how many real zeros the function has and approximate the value of each one. A shallow window can make the curve look as if it turns back toward the axis.

steps.title: Show the function is monotone
steps.explanation: The derivative is always positive, so f rises strictly and can cross the x-axis at most once.
steps.why: Strict monotonicity caps the number of zeros, which is exactly the question a graph alone cannot settle.

steps.title: Prove a zero exists and bracket it
steps.explanation: A continuous function that changes sign on [-1, 0] must vanish somewhere in that interval, and by Step 1 that is the only zero.
steps.why: Existence plus uniqueness turns the visual crossing into a certified single root.

steps.title: Refine numerically
steps.explanation: Zooming the window to [-1, 0] by [-0.1, 0.1] or using the solver's root command brackets the crossing between -0.683 and -0.682, so x approximately -0.6823 to four decimal places.
steps.why: Bracketing the sign change to three decimal places is how graphing software converts a picture into usable numerical accuracy.
